config.text:
Facility Operations Swarm — reference workflow for agent runtime development.

Exercises: input guardrail (pass/fail), JSON LLM extraction into flow variables, rule branching, an HTTP node,
a five-member swarm (four agents + one LLM member, entry point, limits and repetitive-handoff detection),
MCP database tools (PostgreSQL, connection 'sample_open_data') and MCP API tools (NYC Open Data, OpenFEMA),
a script node, an approval with approved/rejected branches, human input, a variable node, an HTML view and outputs.

Data: backend/db/sample_open_data (load with backend/scripts/load_sample_open_data.py).
Docs: docs/strands-builder/runbooks/facility-operations-swarm.md

messages.content:
Extract the scope of a facility operations question. Return ONLY a JSON object:

{
  "intent": "definition" | "investigation",
  "facilityName": "",
  "utilityType": "",
  "periodStart": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "periodEnd": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "includeRisk": true | false,
  "referencePeriodStart": "",
  "referencePeriodEnd": ""
}

Rules:
- intent is "definition" when the user only asks what a term means (for example "what is an HCF?"), otherwise "investigation".
- utilityType is a comma-separated subset of: Electricity, Natural Gas, Water. Empty when not mentioned.
- facilityName is the facility named by the user (for example "Red Hook East"); empty when none.
- When no period is given, use the last full calendar quarter before today ({{system.currentDate}}).
- referencePeriodStart / referencePeriodEnd: the same period one year earlier, unless the user names other comparison periods (at most three, comma-separated).
- includeRisk is true when the user mentions risk, resilience, disasters, storms, floods or insurance.

config.systemPrompt:
The team: coordinator plans and delegates; energy_analyst reads utility bills; facility_analyst profiles facilities and benchmarks them; risk_analyst reviews disaster exposure; report_writer writes the final report. Hand off by name and say exactly what you need back. Never invent numbers: every figure must come from a tool result. Facility data is open test data (NYC Housing Authority, NYC Open Data; FEMA).

You are the coordinator and receive the task first.
1. Restate the question and the scope you were given (facility, utility type, period, reference period).
2. Hand off to energy_analyst for cost and consumption, to facility_analyst for the facility profile and benchmark, and to risk_analyst only when includeRisk is true.
3. When the specialists have reported, hand off to report_writer with a short brief: the question, the key findings and any data gaps.
Do not write the report yourself.

config.systemPrompt:
The team: coordinator plans and delegates; energy_analyst reads utility bills; facility_analyst profiles facilities and benchmarks them; risk_analyst reviews disaster exposure; report_writer writes the final report. Hand off by name and say exactly what you need back. Never invent numbers: every figure must come from a tool result. Facility data is open test data (NYC Housing Authority, NYC Open Data; FEMA).

You are the energy analyst. Use get_utility_bills_with_historical_data for the period against the reference period(s); use get_utility_bills_tool when no reference period is set.
Report per facility and utility type: total expense (USD), total consumption with its unit, the change against each reference period in percent, and bills with zero or estimated charges.
Flag any change above 20 percent. Hand your findings back to coordinator.

configuredTools.name: get_utility_bills_tool
configuredTools.description: Utility bills (cost and consumption) of the user's facilities that overlap the period.
configuredTools.script:
-- get_utility_bills_tool — PostgreSQL, schema sample_open_data (open test data).
--
-- Port of the SQL Server tool of the same name (BNDW.Utility.Bill). Same
-- <placeholders>, same result columns, same filters:
--   <userID>, <newPeriodStart>, <newPeriodEnd>  required
--   <account>, <facilityName>, <region>, <subRegion>, <utilityType>
--       optional, comma-separated; empty or unreplaced means "no filter";
--       facilityName matches a part of the name, the others the whole value,
--       all case-insensitively.
-- Returns the bills of the user's facilities that overlap the period.

WITH p AS (
    SELECT
        sample_open_data.required_bigint('<userID>', 'userID')               AS user_id,
        sample_open_data.required_date('<newPeriodStart>', 'newPeriodStart') AS period_start,
        sample_open_data.required_date('<newPeriodEnd>', 'newPeriodEnd')     AS period_end,
        sample_open_data.param_list('<account>')                             AS accounts,
        sample_open_data.param_list('<facilityName>')                        AS facility_names,
        sample_open_data.param_list('<region>')                              AS regions,
        sample_open_data.param_list('<subRegion>')                           AS sub_regions,
        sample_open_data.param_list('<utilityType>')                         AS utility_types
)
SELECT
    p.user_id                AS "UserID",
    b.bill_sk                AS "BillSk",
    b.facility_sk            AS "FacilitySk",
    f.facility_name          AS "FacilityName",
    f.client_code            AS "ClientCode",
    f.region                 AS "Region",
    f.division               AS "SubRegion",
    b.measurement_code       AS "MeasurementCode",
    b.measurement_unit_code  AS "MeasurementUnitCode",
    b.bill_date              AS "BillDate",
    b.period_start           AS "PeriodStart",
    b.period_end             AS "PeriodEnd",
    b.account                AS "Account",
    b.utility_meter          AS "UtilityMeter",
    b.utility_type           AS "Utility_Type",
    b.expense                AS "Expense",
    b.consumption            AS "Consumption",
    b.currency_abbr          AS "Currency_Abbr",
    b.vendor_sk              AS "VendorSk"
FROM p
JOIN sample_open_data.user_facility_mapping AS m ON m.user_id = p.user_id
JOIN sample_open_data.bill AS b ON b.facility_sk = m.facility_sk
JOIN sample_open_data.facility AS f ON f.facility_sk = b.facility_sk
WHERE b.period_start <= p.period_end
  AND b.period_end >= p.period_start
  AND (p.accounts IS NULL OR lower(b.account) = ANY (p.accounts))
  AND (p.facility_names IS NULL
       OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM unnest(p.facility_names) AS n WHERE lower(f.facility_name) LIKE '%' || n || '%'))
  AND (p.regions IS NULL OR lower(f.region) = ANY (p.regions))
  AND (p.sub_regions IS NULL OR lower(f.division) = ANY (p.sub_regions))
  AND (p.utility_types IS NULL OR lower(b.utility_type) = ANY (p.utility_types))
ORDER BY f.facility_name, b.account, b.measurement_code, b.period_start;

configuredTools.name: get_utility_bills_with_historical_data
configuredTools.description: The same bills, each compared with the matching bills of up to three reference periods.
configuredTools.script:
-- get_utility_bills_with_historical_data — PostgreSQL, schema sample_open_data.
--
-- Port of the SQL Server tool of the same name. Same <placeholders>, same
-- result columns:
--   <userID>, <newPeriodStart>, <newPeriodEnd>  required
--   <historicalReferencePeriodStart>, <historicalReferencePeriodEnd>
--       comma-separated date lists, up to three reference periods
--   <account>, <facilityName>, <region>, <subRegion>, <utilityType>
--       optional filters, as in get_utility_bills_tool
--
-- Each current bill is compared with the bills of the same facility, account,
-- measurement and utility type that overlap the same relative window inside
-- each reference period (the current bill's offset from the period start,
-- applied to the reference period start); their expense and consumption are
-- summed into Ref1..Ref3.

WITH p AS (
    SELECT
        sample_open_data.required_bigint('<userID>', 'userID')               AS user_id,
        sample_open_data.required_date('<newPeriodStart>', 'newPeriodStart') AS period_start,
        sample_open_data.required_date('<newPeriodEnd>', 'newPeriodEnd')     AS period_end,
        sample_open_data.param_list('<account>')                             AS accounts,
        sample_open_data.param_list('<facilityName>')                        AS facility_names,
        sample_open_data.param_list('<region>')                              AS regions,
        sample_open_data.param_list('<subRegion>')                           AS sub_regions,
        sample_open_data.param_list('<utilityType>')                         AS utility_types
),
refs AS (
    SELECT * FROM sample_open_data.reference_periods(
        '<historicalReferencePeriodStart>', '<historicalReferencePeriodEnd>')
),
current_bills AS (
    SELECT b.*, f.facility_name, f.region, f.division
    FROM p
    JOIN sample_open_data.user_facility_mapping AS m ON m.user_id = p.user_id
    JOIN sample_open_data.bill AS b ON b.facility_sk = m.facility_sk
    JOIN sample_open_data.facility AS f ON f.facility_sk = b.facility_sk
    WHERE b.period_start <= p.period_end
      AND b.period_end >= p.period_start
      AND (p.accounts IS NULL OR lower(b.account) = ANY (p.accounts))
      AND (p.facility_names IS NULL
           OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM unnest(p.facility_names) AS n WHERE lower(f.facility_name) LIKE '%' || n || '%'))
      AND (p.regions IS NULL OR lower(f.region) = ANY (p.regions))
      AND (p.sub_regions IS NULL OR lower(f.division) = ANY (p.sub_regions))
      AND (p.utility_types IS NULL OR lower(b.utility_type) = ANY (p.utility_types))
),
historical AS (
    SELECT
        cb.bill_sk,
        r.ref_index,
        r.ref_year,
        r.ref_start,
        r.ref_end,
        w.target_start,
        w.target_end,
        sum(hb.expense)     AS expense,
        sum(hb.consumption) AS consumption
    FROM current_bills AS cb
    CROSS JOIN p
    CROSS JOIN refs AS r
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT r.ref_start + (cb.period_start - p.period_start) AS target_start,
               r.ref_start + (cb.period_end - p.period_start)   AS target_end
    ) AS w
    JOIN sample_open_data.bill AS hb
      ON hb.facility_sk = cb.facility_sk
     AND lower(hb.account) = lower(cb.account)
     AND hb.measurement_code = cb.measurement_code
     AND hb.measurement_unit_code = cb.measurement_unit_code
     AND hb.utility_type = cb.utility_type
     AND hb.period_start <= w.target_end
     AND hb.period_end >= w.target_start
    GROUP BY cb.bill_sk, r.ref_index, r.ref_year, r.ref_start, r.ref_end, w.target_start, w.target_end
),
pivot AS (
    SELECT
        bill_sk,
        max(ref_year)     FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 1) AS ref1_year,
        max(ref_start)    FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 1) AS ref1_start,
        max(ref_end)      FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 1) AS ref1_end,
        max(target_start) FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 1) AS ref1_target_start,
        max(target_end)   FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 1) AS ref1_target_end,
        max(expense)      FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 1) AS ref1_expense,
        max(consumption)  FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 1) AS ref1_consumption,
        max(ref_year)     FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 2) AS ref2_year,
        max(ref_start)    FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 2) AS ref2_start,
        max(ref_end)      FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 2) AS ref2_end,
        max(target_start) FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 2) AS ref2_target_start,
        max(target_end)   FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 2) AS ref2_target_end,
        max(expense)      FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 2) AS ref2_expense,
        max(consumption)  FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 2) AS ref2_consumption,
        max(ref_year)     FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 3) AS ref3_year,
        max(ref_start)    FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 3) AS ref3_start,
        max(ref_end)      FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 3) AS ref3_end,
        max(target_start) FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 3) AS ref3_target_start,
        max(target_end)   FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 3) AS ref3_target_end,
        max(expense)      FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 3) AS ref3_expense,
        max(consumption)  FILTER (WHERE ref_index = 3) AS ref3_consumption
    FROM historical
    GROUP BY bill_sk
)
SELECT
    p.user_id                 AS "UserID",
    cb.bill_sk                AS "BillSk",
    cb.facility_sk            AS "FacilitySk",
    cb.facility_name          AS "FacilityName",
    cb.region                 AS "Region",
    cb.division               AS "SubRegion",
    cb.measurement_code       AS "MeasurementCode",
    cb.measurement_unit_code  AS "MeasurementUnitCode",
    cb.bill_date              AS "BillDate",
    cb.period_start           AS "PeriodStart",
    cb.period_end             AS "PeriodEnd",
    cb.account                AS "Account",
    cb.utility_meter          AS "UtilityMeter",
    cb.utility_type           AS "Utility_Type",
    cb.expense                AS "Expense",
    cb.consumption            AS "Consumption",
    cb.currency_abbr          AS "Currency_Abbr",
    cb.vendor_sk              AS "VendorSk",
    hp.ref1_year              AS "Ref1_Year",
    hp.ref1_start             AS "Ref1_PeriodStart",
    hp.ref1_end               AS "Ref1_PeriodEnd",
    hp.ref1_target_start      AS "Ref1_TargetPeriodStart",
    hp.ref1_target_end        AS "Ref1_TargetPeriodEnd",
    hp.ref1_expense           AS "Expense_Ref1",
    hp.ref1_consumption       AS "Consumption_Ref1",
    hp.ref2_year              AS "Ref2_Year",
    hp.ref2_start             AS "Ref2_PeriodStart",
    hp.ref2_end               AS "Ref2_PeriodEnd",
    hp.ref2_target_start      AS "Ref2_TargetPeriodStart",
    hp.ref2_target_end        AS "Ref2_TargetPeriodEnd",
    hp.ref2_expense           AS "Expense_Ref2",
    hp.ref2_consumption       AS "Consumption_Ref2",
    hp.ref3_year              AS "Ref3_Year",
    hp.ref3_start             AS "Ref3_PeriodStart",
    hp.ref3_end               AS "Ref3_PeriodEnd",
    hp.ref3_target_start      AS "Ref3_TargetPeriodStart",
    hp.ref3_target_end        AS "Ref3_TargetPeriodEnd",
    hp.ref3_expense           AS "Expense_Ref3",
    hp.ref3_consumption       AS "Consumption_Ref3"
FROM current_bills AS cb
CROSS JOIN p
LEFT JOIN pivot AS hp ON hp.bill_sk = cb.bill_sk
ORDER BY cb.facility_name, cb.account, cb.measurement_code, cb.period_start;

nodes.name: facility_analyst
nodes.description: Profiles facilities and benchmarks their electricity cost against other developments

config.systemPrompt:
The team: coordinator plans and delegates; energy_analyst reads utility bills; facility_analyst profiles facilities and benchmarks them; risk_analyst reviews disaster exposure; report_writer writes the final report. Hand off by name and say exactly what you need back. Never invent numbers: every figure must come from a tool result. Facility data is open test data (NYC Housing Authority, NYC Open Data; FEMA).

You are the facility analyst. Use facility_profile for the facilities in scope (borough, county, bill coverage) and nyc_electricity_benchmark to place them against other NYCHA developments.
Report each facility's rank in the benchmark and any gaps in bill coverage. Hand your findings back to coordinator.

configuredTools.name: facility_profile
configuredTools.description: The user's facilities with borough, county and bill coverage.
configuredTools.script:
-- facility_profile: the facilities a user may see, with their bill coverage.
SELECT
    f.facility_sk, f.facility_name, f.borough, f.county, f.region, f.division AS sub_region,
    f.amp, f.funding_source,
    count(b.bill_sk)            AS bill_count,
    min(b.period_start)         AS first_period,
    max(b.period_end)           AS last_period,
    array_agg(DISTINCT b.utility_type) FILTER (WHERE b.utility_type IS NOT NULL) AS utility_types
FROM sample_open_data.user_facility_mapping m
JOIN sample_open_data.facility f ON f.facility_sk = m.facility_sk
LEFT JOIN sample_open_data.bill b ON b.facility_sk = f.facility_sk
WHERE m.user_id = sample_open_data.required_bigint('<userID>', 'userID')
  AND (sample_open_data.param_list('<facilityName>') IS NULL
       OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM unnest(sample_open_data.param_list('<facilityName>')) n
                  WHERE lower(f.facility_name) LIKE '%' || n || '%'))
GROUP BY f.facility_sk
ORDER BY f.facility_name;

nodes.description: Assesses disaster exposure of the facilities' counties from FEMA declarations

config.systemPrompt:
The team: coordinator plans and delegates; energy_analyst reads utility bills; facility_analyst profiles facilities and benchmarks them; risk_analyst reviews disaster exposure; report_writer writes the final report. Hand off by name and say exactly what you need back. Never invent numbers: every figure must come from a tool result. Facility data is open test data (NYC Housing Authority, NYC Open Data; FEMA).

You are the risk analyst. Use facility_disasters for the facilities' counties and openfema_recent_ny_declarations for what is happening now.
Summarise the incident types, how recent they are, and which facilities share an exposed county. Rate exposure low, medium or high with a one-line reason. Hand your findings back to coordinator.

configuredTools.name: facility_disasters
configuredTools.description: Disasters declared in the counties of the user's facilities, last 15 years.
configuredTools.script:
-- facility_disasters: FEMA declarations for the counties of the user's facilities.
SELECT
    d.facility_name, d.borough, d.county, d.disaster_number, d.declaration_type, d.incident_type,
    d.declaration_title, d.declaration_date, d.incident_begin_date, d.incident_end_date,
    d.ia_program_declared, d.pa_program_declared, d.hm_program_declared
FROM sample_open_data.v_facility_disaster d
JOIN sample_open_data.user_facility_mapping m ON m.facility_sk = d.facility_sk
WHERE m.user_id = sample_open_data.required_bigint('<userID>', 'userID')
  AND (sample_open_data.param_list('<facilityName>') IS NULL
       OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM unnest(sample_open_data.param_list('<facilityName>')) n
                  WHERE lower(d.facility_name) LIKE '%' || n || '%'))
  AND d.declaration_date >= (current_date - interval '15 years')
ORDER BY d.declaration_date DESC, d.facility_name
LIMIT 200;

nodes.name: report_writer
nodes.description: Writes the final Markdown report and its severity line

messages.content:
The team: coordinator plans and delegates; energy_analyst reads utility bills; facility_analyst profiles facilities and benchmarks them; risk_analyst reviews disaster exposure; report_writer writes the final report. Hand off by name and say exactly what you need back. Never invent numbers: every figure must come from a tool result. Facility data is open test data (NYC Housing Authority, NYC Open Data; FEMA).

You are the report writer and finish the task; do not hand off.
Write a concise Markdown report: a title, an executive summary (three bullets), Energy, Facilities, Risk (when analysed), Data gaps, and Recommended actions.
End with exactly one line:
SEVERITY: <0-10>
where 10 means urgent action is needed (for example costs up more than 50 percent, or high disaster exposure).
